statement: The PRC declares national reunification to be its objective and describes peaceful reunification as its preferred path.
PRC law identifies three broad conditions under which state authorities shall employ nonpeaceful means, while leaving operational thresholds indeterminate.
PRC official policy treats Taiwan independence and external interference as linked political threats.
The August 2022 exercise publicly demonstrated joint blockade, strike, air control, and live fire subjects around Taiwan.
The April 2023 Joint Sword event continued an encircling joint patrol and exercise pattern.
Joint Sword 2024A involved Army, Navy, Air Force, and Rocket Force exercise activity around Taiwan and nearby islands.
Joint Sword 2024B publicly emphasized port and area blockade, maritime and land attack, and comprehensive superiority.
The April 2025 sequence included joint exercises and Strait Thunder subjects spanning identification, expulsion, interception, detention, regional control, blockade, and precision strike.
Taiwan recorded 59 PLA aircraft sorties, 23 PLAN ships, and 8 official ships during the 2 to 3 April 2025 reporting window; these are activity observations, not unique force inventory totals.
Taiwan recorded 57 PLA aircraft sorties, 6 PLAN ships, and 4 official ships during the 7 to 8 August 2025 reporting window; these are activity observations, not unique force inventory totals.
The safely prebookmark 29 and 31 August public reports show variation in aircraft activity alongside continuing aggregate naval and official ship reporting.

The last public daily report established as available before the bookmark reported 5 aircraft sorties, 6 PLAN ships, and 1 official ship. These are Taiwan public-report activity instances, not unique platforms or omniscient truth.
Taiwan publicly described an integrated ISR response supported by mission aircraft, vessels, and shore based missile systems in the safely prebookmark April report.
Han Kuang 41 rehearsed continuous joint defense, civil military coordination, decentralization, force protection, mobilization, and gray zone transition response.

United States law treats nonpeaceful determination of Taiwan’s future, including boycott or embargo, as grave concern and directs defensive assistance and maintenance of capacity to resist force or coercion.
The Taiwan Relations Act does not itself encode automatic United States combat entry for every Taiwan crisis.
notes: This is a legal scope observation, not a forecast of United States behavior.

statement: Standing United States presence in Japan is not modeled as automatic mission permission for every Taiwan contingency.
EDCA access and alliance consultation are not modeled as automatic offensive mission permission for every Taiwan contingency.
Public exercises demonstrate practiced mission categories but do not establish complete wartime readiness, sustainability, or probability of success.
Organization identity and public activity counts do not establish deployment, readiness, access, or theater availability; all four remain explicit unknowns.
